memory_candidates.content: When a review cites a Lean declaration found only in prose (task descriptions, ROADMAP rows, prior reports), grep the tree for the bare name before transcribing it: in this repository `verifyProof` was cited by a task description, the ROADMAP and a research report yet exists nowhere in FormalSystem/. Stale names propagate through specs/ because each surface copies the previous one; a `grep -rn <name> FormalSystem/` costs seconds and is the only check that catches it.

Hypothesis sweeps over markdown must be paragraph- or table-row-aware, not line-aware: a qualifier such as `[F.IsRegular]` or `(ValidZTime φ)` routinely wraps to the next line of a hard-wrapped sentence, so a same-line grep reports false positives. Split on blank lines, treat each `|`-leading table line as its own unit, and check the qualifier within that unit.
